text_fidelity_a:
Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX Update 8-7-19: I went to the WD website to register my two drives. They show as no warranty from WD, presumably because they were bought through a reseller. Just so you know ...

I use these as primary storage (and backup storage) for our MacBook Air laptop. Most MacBooks now come with solid state drives, meaning memory chip based drives, not physical spinning disks. They are much more expensive than the heritage physical disk approach, such that the largest SSD that we could get with our 2017 MacBook Air was a 256 GB drive. These WD Black (virtually enterprise level) drives are 500 GB each, so our storage is 2x that of the built in drive. We use one as our primary external drive; once a month we install the 2nd drive (also externally), copy the files across, and put it into our safe deposit box at the bank. If we ever lose a drive, whether to failure or someone breaking in and stealing our drive and laptop, we're only 30 days behind, a real advantage.

The only downside to this drive is that the warranty on the drive itself is provided by the Seller, OEMGENUINE. The drive came marked with a label on the drive as a Seller 5 year warranty, with no terms provided. The downside risk is there is no published warranty, either by the Seller or by WD on their website, and whatever warranty is provided is subject to the Seller still being in existence over the next 5 years. However, given the price of the drive ($35 or so), it was a reasonable risk to take, especially since we acquired two and use one as the backup to the primary one. The odds of losing two drives at the same time is pretty remote. So we accepted the risk, but dropped the review for the product & seller by 1 star. If you go to the WD website, they do claim a 5 year limited warranty. I am a little surprised that the WD website doesn't provide a link to their warranty. So if we can't reach OEMGENUINE should we have a problem, I'm not sure what protection we'll have from WD. Something to consider if that's important to you.

These are fast drives (7200 rpm for the 500GB drive), which is noticeably faster than the previous bulk drives we've purchased online and/or removed from existing systems, which have all been 5400 rpm drives. SATA compatible, plug and play, no issues yet but it's only been a few days. If something materially changes, I'll post an update.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 320GB WD Black Performance Mobile Hard Drive - 7200 RPM Class, SATA 6 Gb/s, , 32 MB Cache, 2.5" - WD3200LPLX

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black) Boy! does this camera remind me of my old Polaroid Square Shooter. This camera is NOTHING like your iPhone camera as it's big, and totally analog except for the film counter on the back. I love it when the motor runs and film comes sliding out - a sound I well remember. I think the hardest thing about using this camera was getting the shoulder strap put on, other than that it's very easy to use. Though it is on the big side, it doesn't weigh much and the view finder and shutter button are pretty much intuitive. I'm left handed so holding it like a right-hander took a little getting used too, but it's not a problem for me. This camera is made for right-handers so those who are very much left-handed might not like the way you have to hold it, and the shutter button is on the right side front. It has flash and you can adjust the light/dark and distance to you subject with minimal effort.

Loading the film was easy, aiming at my subject was easy, the shutter button was easy to depress and everything is/was easy. The close-up adapter looks like there's no way it will attach itself to the lens, but somehow it does. I took one close-up of my dog but the picture didn't turn out very good because she moved away right when I hit the shutter button-but that's typical for her. I haven't taken a "selfie" yet but it seems like it will be easy to do.

The color development of the film is pretty good. I took a wide angle picture of my raised garden beds and I was able to get all of them in the picture and the various green colors were vivid. I also took a picture of the front of our house, and though I had to still walk across the street to our neighbor's driveway to get the entire house in the view finder, the picture turned out nice. Again, the colors were bright and vivid. It got the entire house plus some area on both sides. In the past with my other cameras I would have to get further away or be happy with just most of the house in the picture so it's real nice to get the whole thing with room to spare.

The film is kind of pricey. For a pack of 40 pictures it costs around $34.00. I figured it would be kind of expensive and I hope the price of the film goes down some. This is a comfort camera for those of us who grew up with Polaroids. It may be that since we are living in highly uncertain and stressful times, having a camera like this is a cool blast from the past and may make us just feel better having one like this, plus it takes nice pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black This is my first purchase of earbuds in the over $200 category. I got the Jabra Elite 65t as soon as they came out and have since bought a couple of other pairs of earbuds in the under $100 category that had better features like IPX7 or 8hr battery life. Therefore I was excited to upgrade to the XM4 for their bettery life and the noise canceling.

Unfortunately, I've had several issues with these. I don't have particularly small ears. Usually the medium tips fit without issue. On the XM4, I started with the medium tips and tested their air tightness using the app. The small tips don't have any kind of seal on my ears without really shoving them super far down my ear canal, so I decided to stick with the medium size. Unfortunately, I have experienced significant ear fatigue enough so that I can't wear the earbuds for more than a couple of hours. I have since switched to the small tips for the sake of comfort, but that means sacrificing any passive noise canceling - and unless I have a defective unit, without the passive noise canceling in addition to the active noise canceling, there is absolutely no difference between having the noise canceling on and off. To me, this completely defeats the purpose of buying noise canceling earbuds.

I also have had issues with connectivity such as the bluetooth connection on my phone suddenly dropping and having to go into the app to manually pair them again.

In terms of battery life, depending on the control settings of each earbud, there can be a difference in the drain of battery between the left and right side. On a bad day, I had a 30% difference with the right draining significantly faster. My earbuds are using the factory settings with the playback controls on the right and the noise canceling on the left for reference.

Both the connectivity problems and the bettery difference between the earbuds has seemed to have gotten better since performing a factory reset, but be aware that there is still a little difference in the rate of battery drain between the L and R earbuds (It's not super significant now and maybe reaches under 7-8% difference at the end of the day).

I bought some Comply foam tips, which I hope will fix the discomfort issue and make the noise canceling work at the optimal rate without the ear fatigue. However, I shouldn't have to modify almost $300 earbuds to make them work like they should. It would help if Sony would offer more sizes of ear tips to help make them more usable for a wider population. Then again, if I have gripes like these, then maybe the XM4s aren't for me. Makes me super sad considering I think that they're probably fantastic for most people.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black

I guess, since you're really only using this for electronics with rectifiers built in, you really don't need it to be grounded. It is a shame, in that case, that the stupid UK/Middle-East plug has to have the dielectric prong instead of the ground because a lot of their outlets are tamper resistant (but that is not this product's fault).

Speaking of UK plugs and their bulk, this device isn't really all that big when you're used to carrying some UK adapters around anyway. And now you also don't really need your five volt power adapters.

You can usually force a "European plug" (this one is like an ungrounded Schuko plug) into the lower amperage (smaller) Italian socket (and you can often rest an ungrounded, lower amperage, Italian plug into a Schuko or other Euro outlet), but it is not ideal, and I actually don't want to put that kind of stress on a $20 product (whereas throwaway adapters are okay for this purpose). Italians sometimes have mainland or combo outlets in their hotels, but it would be more ideal if a proper Italian plug and outlet was included in this device yet. I mean, it's just Italy, but everyone wants to go there, and I happen to have work there, so that would make this more ideal. Truth is, I'll probably always carry various extra adapters anyway.

USB ports can do .85amps each if they're all being used, but the truth is that I have a lot of old USB chargers that only do 500mA, so everything will charge, maybe just slowly if you have them all used. But each port can do 2.4a if used individually.

Overall, it's the coolest and most inclusive such adapter that I've seen.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy NX EK-GN120ZKAXAR Galaxy Wireless Smart Android 4G Camera 20.3MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 4.8-Inch LCD with 18-55mm OIS Lens (Black) Just opening the box is a joy, making this a great gift. Instead of the usual plastic and white or brown packing, all is in a beautifully designed chic black, with every item showcased to perfection.
Easy set up, right out of the box. I bought the [[ASIN:B00C7EPVHY Samsung Galaxy Camera with Android Jelly Bean v4.2 OS, 16.3MP CMOS with 21x Optical Zoom and 4.8" Touch Screen LCD (WiFi - White)]]a few months ago (also a great camera if you don't want to mess with a cell service for your camera) so it took no time at all, but even if you're an android newbie, it's still simple and straightforward. The Samsung website has some terrific videos showing various features. After an initial get-to-know-ya with this camera, check out more cool things you can do. Also, I myself find it helpful in the beginning to download the PDF of the manual and print off parts I want. The whole manual is over 200 pages, so I just print off what I need.

And even if you're relatively new to photography you'll feel like a pro with an easy to change lens. And about the lens, WOW! Looking at this camera? Get the model that includes the lens! More about the lens later...I could not be more excited!

The Optical Image Stabilizer in the 18-55mm lens offers clear, sharp images. The NX System lens incorporates i-Function Technology which lets you control the camera from the lens itself. It provides one step control of the shutter speed.
The AF (Auto Focus) is fast at 0.17 (!!!) seconds so it easily catches up to your next shot.
Recently, I was photographing an awards ceremony. The 'money shot', of course, was the transfer of the award. My darn camera took so long to autofocus from the previous shot, I missed it. Got a second before, a second after. That will never happen again.
And this is really cool...put the viewfinder up to your eye, and the touchscreen is disabled so your face isn't interfere with the screen icons.

The GPS tracker enables photographers to capture their exact geographical location in real time.

I'm already picking out the goodies to add to this camera. Samsung has a 10mm Fisheye lens, a 20mm pancake lens for taking great landscapes and an 18-200mm zoom...jeez, too many to mention that can be purchased separately. There are a lot of NX cases on eBay, if you want the 'real' one, when I looked, it was cheaper via Amazon versus the Samsung website.
You can also get external flash, remote switch, microphone.

This is THE camera, and the future of all cameras. It's easy enough for a budding photographer, slick enough for the pro.

Any other questions or anything you WISH this review had, just click the 'comment' button below and I'll do whatever I can to help, be it a video, research, whatever. I love it and am happy to share whatever I can so that you can decide if it's right for you.

UPDATE EDIT 3/4/14: The features and options never seem to end on this camera! It can get complicated, but thankfully Samsung has a dedicated support line for it. I've called twice with questions, never had to wait too long. Because this product is so new, if they don't know what youre talking about, ask to be switched to 'professional camera equipment' NOT 'digital camera'.
I feel like there are no stupid questions, only stupid answers, so I admit I asked some stupid questions. They were explained with enough information that I could look up and research the rest.
Since I am NOT a lifelong camera person, some features that would be 101 to others were new to me. And I'm so glad I had the Galaxy with Android Jelly Bean v4.2 OS, 16.3MP first.
The more I peek into what it can do, the more excited I am. One thing I should clarify about my review...I say it is fine for a budding photographer, and it is, but if you just want something to take photos or movies that is point and shoot, you won't be taking advantage of it's full potential. This is a camera for geeks and tech junkies! If you are a newbie, but have the DESIRE, this can be a first pro camera.
There is nothing else like this out there right now.

Someone asked about a 'zoom button'. Like any professional camera, you zoom with the lens, you WANT to zoom with the lens. Part of what is cutting edge about this camera is the way the lens 'talks' to the camera. The information about the functionality of the lens is sent to the body of the camera, so that any options that you have to control the lens shows up on the screen. Each additional lens you may choose to add has different functionality...screen options CHANGE with each lens because the camera KNOWS which lens is on. This is HUGE!
NEVER has this been done before, and I believe it will change the art of photography.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy NX EK-GN120ZKAXAR Galaxy Wireless Smart Android 4G Camera 20.3MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 4.8-Inch LCD with 18-55mm OIS Lens (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) I made absolutely sure everything was closed before putting it into water, not that one could have much faith in the mechanisms keeping it closed, as they are easy to accidentally open. I put it in the water gently, and only a foot or so, to film some stingrays and fish; this recording went fine. Later that day, I wanted to photograph a tiny little crab. I took one picture from above the water, and one from below. I noticed this time, when I put the camera underwater, that bubbles started to come out the top. I immediately took it out and noticed the screen starting to fog up with condensation and moisture, the first very bad sign. I double checked everything was still closed, and it was. No part of it had been opened. I put it back in, hoping for the best. After coming back to the sand (never having done more than a few feet underwater), I tried to turn it on to get some video. It would not turn on. I checked again, and nothing appeared to be open. I then dried the exterior and opened it, only to discover there was water on the inside. I immediately removed the SD card, in hopes of salvaging it, but the camera was (is) completely dead.

Two days later, there is corrosion forming on the inside from the water, but at least I salvaged the content on the SD card. The results? Video quality is fine above and below water. Photo quality is a mess. Absolutely the worst pics imaginable.
I am so glad I didn't have to pay for this product; I would have been furious it didn't even last a day in the ocean.

I expected more, since I had previously purchased a "Kodak EasyShare Sport C123 12 MP Waterproof Digital Camera", which has been great! That product never failed after much abuse and takes decent picture and video. I'm not sure what happened here, but buyer beware! Try the EasyShare Sport instead.

I'll post some pictures and, if it lets me, some video too. I hope you all find this helpful!

UPDATE: I can't post video (sorry)
Also, I looked at some other reviews that mentioned water getting in while at the pool or in other non-salinated water. Bear in mind that many electronics can survive water immersion if it is fresh water (as opposed to salt water). Many of these reviewers gave the camera more than one star because it was able to work again, but bear in mind this will NOT hold true it Salt water enters the device. Please consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Dolby Audio, Dual-Band Wi-Fi, 32 GB (Previous Generation - 2nd) SEE BELOW FOR LATEST ON 5-3-13
SEE BELOW FOR LATEST ON 5-11-13 SECOND DEVICE GOING BACK TOO. SOUND FAILED.
SEE BELOW FOR FINAL REVIEW, ALL POSITIVE, 5-20-13

5-11-13 I REALLY DON'T KNOW HOW TO RATE THIS THING NOW. WHEN IT RUNS IT IS FINE. WHEN IT DOESN'T IT ISN'T. NOW THE SOUND HAS FAILED. CAN'T RUN PANDORA, ANY WEBSITE THAT PLAYS AN AUDIO TRACK WITH VIDEO OR MUSIC; CAN'T RUN MP3 OR MP4 FILES AND HEAR ANY SOUND. ANOTHER BEING SHIPPED TO ARRIVE HERE TUESDAY. I AM GETTING REALLY TIRED OF REBUILDING MY BOOKMARKS, APPS, PREFERENCES, ETC. I HAVE WASTED HOURS AND HOURS DOING THIS NOW. I WAS EVEN SO HAPPY THIS TIME THAT I BOUGHT MY WIFE A 7" FIRE HD FOR MOTHER'S DAY. I PRAY HER'S WORKS. I HAVE ALMOST COMPLETELY LOST MY FAITH IN FIRE HD.

The above, and the stuff I deleted from my first review had to do with screen flaws in the first and dead sound card in second. All cleared up and the cogent review comes next.

5-20-13

PROBLEMS RESOLVED WITH THIRD DEVICE. WHEN THEY WORK AND WITH SOME APPS TO SPEED THINGS UP, IT IS 5 STARS NOW.

While waiting for the 3rd device I checked around the web for quality issues with other vendors and discovered they all have problems now. The race to grab some market share is pushing new/re-designed devices out too fast and DOA and other issues are rampant in the industry. Amazom actually may be a bit better; the offset is that if you have a problem and get on the phone with them it is pretty easy to get a new device sent out for exchange via 2-day air, and you keep the one you have until the new arrives. That is an industry high mark that not all vendors have. So this took a lot of the sting out of flaws. Enough.

The device is beautiful, powerful and in 32 GB size has enough memory for most of us, even the video users or gamers who save lots of bytes.

I made the best change though by installing the Dolphin browser app and ES File Explorer. Doplpin is faster than Silk and more flexible. Also you can organzie folders for bookmarks very easily. ES File Exp is a tool you need. You can find almost everything on your device easily and manage apps and other files. They are both free and in Amazon store.

I use Last Pass and Xmarks to manage passwords and bookmarks on desktop/laptop machines and they both work very well with Dolphin. So I was able to load a lot of bookmarks easily that otherwise would have been typed in laboriously and taken hours.

I use Gmail because that gives me the perfect multi-platform email program.

I am a Latin student and found a couple of very good Latin apps. I also was able to find The Daily Missal Readings and an app with the Liturgy of the Hours, in both Latin and English. Both available in Amazon Store too.

When in range of Wifi I can do anything I need to do and do it well with the Kindle Fire HD 8.9" When operating stand-alone I have Latin-English books/Bibles on the device and the necessary dictionaries to continue translation. Very handy.

The only fault still, and I have complained about this repeatedly to Amazon, you can look up a foreign word from a book in German, Spanish, Portugese, French and Italian dictionaries, plus several Oriental tongues, but Latin is not a choice. You have to go to the web or type the word out into Google Translate, Whitaker's Words or some online program. It seems it would be easy to add the Latin dictionary as an option because several very good digital versions are around and I use two of them on an e-ink 1st generation Kindle device. Fix that Kindle and you get 10 stars!

In short, buy one but if you have trouble, get to them right away. Of course, read the instructions and make sure your complaint is not from lack of knowledge.

My final words on the subject.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Dolby Audio, Dual-Band Wi-Fi, 32 GB (Previous Generation - 2nd)

text_fidelity_a:
Denon DSB-250BT Envaya Portable Bluetooth 8.25” Speaker (Black) - Lightweight, Waterproof & Dustproof | Up to 13 Hours of Battery Life | Hands-Free Phone Calling | Voice Compatibility with Siri This is a pricey Bluetooth speaker, but a high quality one so you do get what you pay for here. It’s one of my two favorite ones (the other is the Jam Heavy Metal) and outside of the Jam is far better sound quality than the several others I own. If you’re looking for something that gives you “adequate” music and can handle a splash or two, this is overkill. But if you want rich sound and insurance against big rain (or worse, a dunk in a pool), it’s probably worth moving up to this one.

Pros:
IP67, highly water-resistant. I confess, I didn’t test this by submerging it as it says you can; I’m gonna just trust ‘em on this one

Rich, distortion-free sound. Despite its size, this can get quite loud (in a nice touch for those wishing to pump it up, the volume controls on the speaker, unlike most I own, work independently of your source device (i.e. you can max out your iphone volume and then in addition max out the speaker). Even at high volume the sound doesn’t distort. And the bass is powerful and thick (not sub-woofer but then, if you want that, get a sub-woofer. For a portable speaker, it’s perhaps the best bass I’ve heard). It’s also quite clear. In comparison to the Jam, I’d say the bass on this is better but the Jam just edges out in terms of clarity with treble/voice. The sound quality is also quite good as a speaker phone.

Connecting. Pairing via Bluetooth was pretty instantaneous with my iPhone and iPad. There’s also an audio-jack to plug in

Stereo potential. You can link it with another, though I don’t have a second so can’t speak to how it sounds

Size: it’s small enough to toss easily into a backpack if not a pocket. Has a heft to it in terms of a quality, durable build-feel, but not so as to strain you carrying it around at all.

Cons are all pretty minor
Buttons are a bit stiff (maybe this will change)

No charging cable with mine

Neutral: no connectivity with voice activation like Alexa
Charges in a few hours and last anywhere from 8-12 depending on volume, not the best but far from the worst

Personally, I hate tinny, thin-sounding speakers. If I’m going to listen to music, I don’t need it to be pristine, but I do want it to sound like my music, so I think this is a good value. The sound quality alone is worth it—it blows away cheaper Bluetooth portables— and combined with the high-level water resistance, it’s makes it an even easier recommendation
text_fidelity_b: Denon DSB-250BT Envaya Portable Bluetooth 8.25” Speaker (Black) - Lightweight, Waterproof & Dustproof | Up to 13 Hours of Battery Life | Hands-Free Phone Calling | Voice Compatibility with Siri

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Party Speaker - Wireless PA Speaker with Lights, Radio, Bass Boost, Mic Input and USB Charging ***Updated** 8/13/2019

This speaker was plugged in and fully charged after receiving. I have not been able to get it to charge since. Even when plugged in it turns on, says low battery then immediately turns off.

I removed battery to manually charge (there is a compartment under the speaker). Once removed from charger at 26v, as soon as it was connected to the stereo, voltage dropped to 10v, said low battery again and shut off. This speaker went straight to the trash. I had higher hopes for this speaker. Unfortunately it didn’t last longer than a couple of weeks.

For the size of this speaker, I was expecting much better sound.

With the bass button on, the sound is fairly clear and sounds ok. Bass doesn’t hit as hard as I thought it would. I have another speaker half the size that sounds better than this one (at half the price). Without the bass button turned on, the sound is much lower and no longer allows an equalizer setting to be selected.

To turn on, press and hold power button. BT setup was easy and device will automatically connect to the last paired device upon turning on.

Once charged, this is a wireless speaker. It can be paired to another identical speaker. I don’t need 2 of these so I won’t be doing that. It would be nice if it could be paired to any other BT capable speaker.

There are handles on the sides to make carrying easy.

USB port is convenient for charging your phone or other mp3 device. Microphone port works fine and has its own volume knob.

The light on the speaker isn’t super bright but is annoying during daylight hours. It comes on automatically after the bass button is pressed and has to be manually shut off by pressing the light button 7-8 times (it has to go through each of the light settings before turning off).

This would be alright as a garage speaker or even as a kids karaoke machine but It isn’t something I would want to carry around to parties, nor is the sound something to show off.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Party Speaker - Wireless PA Speaker with Lights, Radio, Bass Boost, Mic Input and USB Charging

Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US Like all dedicated gaming laptops, this is a big heavy high-powered machine. It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US

text_fidelity_a:
Canon 6558B003 EOS Rebel T4i 18-135mm is TM Lens Kit 18MP SLR Camera with 3-Inch LCD Body (Black) I had been borrowing a T3i for the times when I wanted something more lightweight and portable than my 5D Mark II. Given all the time I was spending with the T3i, I thought it was time to get my own.

I was torn between the T3i and the T4i but Amazon made it easy since they were both priced the same before Christmas. So, I went for the T4i, and am very glad I did. It's a nice improvement over the T3i.

The most telling upgrade has been the touch screen. I admit I was a bit wary of this since I'm comfortable with the traditional buttons, menus and rocker switches. After using it for a few days I very much miss having it on my other Canons. Very responsive, allows me to jump to a setting more quickly, and just plain easy and fun to use!

I do have to admit that Canon's claim that this is a "smudge resistant" screen is only partially true. It sort of, kind of resists smudges, but I usually end up cleaning the screen a few times during use.

The other novel feature of the T4i is the ability to have continuous autofocus in movie mode. I'm more of a still photographer than a videographer, so that's does not make a huge impact for me. However, I have used it and it does work very well - I may start shooting more video now, and am considering getting the 40mm STM lens (although the continual autofocus works with any lens, it's best suited with an STM lens).

Most of the specs of the T4i are identical to the T3i; a few have been tweaked, such as a higher frame rate, higher ISO and faster processor.

I was a no-brainer for me to get the T4i when it was priced the same as the T3i. But now that I've had it for a while, I certainly think the added features make it a worthwhile choice over the T3i even at a higher price. It you purchased a T3i recently, it's probably best to wait for the inevitable T5i whenever it comes out rather than upgrade now. But, if you're debating between the T3i and the T4i, go for the 4, if only for the touchscreen.
text_fidelity_b: Canon 6558B003 EOS Rebel T4i 18-135mm is TM Lens Kit 18MP SLR Camera with 3-Inch LCD Body (Black)

I’m also picky about mice, but am trying to be as ergonomic as possible in my peripheral choices, to prevent problems down the road. My current daily driver mouse is Logitech’s MX Master 3 and I use a palm grip.

I’ve wanted to try a vertical mouse since reading about them, but for me, the DELUX Vertical Mouse won’t be the one. The mouse is just too big for my small hand. To give an idea of my hand size, I wear a size small women’s glove.

My hand doesn’t fit naturally on the mouse. My whole hand slides down the body, so I have to keep tension in my hand and arm to keep my fingers in the proper place to be able to use the mouse buttons. It’s not comfortable; my hand and wrist hurt within minutes. My thumb keeps sliding to sit on the bottom of the side buttons, so it’s fortunate for me the side buttons don’t work on Macs.

I tried the mouse with and without the palm rest, there was no difference.

On the plus side, the mouse charges via USB-C, and can connect via Bluetooth or wireless. If you don’t use it, the wireless dongle fits neatly into the base of the mouse without impeding using it.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black) An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.
text_fidelity_b: Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Wicked HD CARDVR1080PWHD4GB 1080p Car Camera & DVR Box (Black) UPDATE 7/13/2017: This dash cam fell off the mount yesterday. I examined it and found the plastic on the top had cracked. This is the ORIGINAL dash cam which still functions well. I am not using the more recent dash cam that Amcrest refused to update (see below for the 4/18/2017 update). Too bad it could not have been manufactured with a metal top or outer casing that would stand up to removing and replacing and repositioning.

The most recent comments (UPDATES) apply to the more recently bought WICKEDHD dash cam that carries the name AMCREST on the box.

UPDATE 4/18/2017 - When I emailed AMCREST about the problems with the camera, I was told on April 11 "Thank you for contacting Amcrest Support, my name is Kirby and I'm the Product Support Specialist here and I will do my best to assist you with any issues or questions you may be having.

We are currently working on an updated for this device. I am very sorry for the inconvenience. I will put your ticket on hold so that I can do a follow up."

Today, 4/18/2017, however, I received this from the same AMCREST person.
"Unfortunately, we no longer service this product. It has been discontinued. I am very sorry for the inconvenience."

So they waited until the 30-day return limit passed before telling me the product is discontinued. Now I am stuck with a dash cam that has to have the date set every time it is powered.

Because of this treatment / experience, I will not be buying any more AMCREST products.

UPDATE 4/9/2017 - Bought another camera, expected it to function as the first one.
HOWEVER, several problems have reared their ugly heads.
1. The date resets to 01/01/2014 whenever it is turned OFF.
2. Recording does not start when the ignition is turned on and power is supplied to the camera. The green light on the plug-in to the DC outlet is ON but the camera will not turn on.
3. Recording of video clips appear to be in one folder; they are not in folders based on the date as they were on previous cameras.

Comments below apply to the older version(s) of the WICKED HD dash cam. I gave those 4 STARS.

UPDATE 11/1/2015 - No problems except for a few stray spots that are on the sensor or the inner lens. A couple of times one 3-minute video was skipped as the recording went from one folder to another on the same uninterrupted trip. The original micro-SD card has remained in the dash cam all these months.
The camera setting is for 1080p video so that license tags in front of me and gas prices and other signs on the sides of the road will be discernible when viewed on my computer. If my vehicle is stopped for a light, the zoom produces images that are clear enough but it is obvious they are pixelated.

UPDATE 3/9/2015 - The company sent me a replacement that arrived today. Unfortunately, the box contains no rearview mirror mount for the dash cam. That will cost me another $10 to order separately.
The good news is that the micro-SD card stayed in - finally - when I inserted it into the memory card slot. That needs to be redesigned such that the mechanism doesn't eject the card as easily as it does. The cut-out doesn't match the lip on the SD card - it's on the opposite side of where it logically should be. The 'manual' simply says the micro SD card should be inserted as in the [non-existant] "image below; press it until you hear a click." No image and no click. The micro SD card doesn't stay in until just the right position is achieved.

After I have used it, I will post any comments as to the images produced. Hopefully the videos won't have the smears / streaks / spots that the first dash cam had.

UPDATE 3/3/2015 - The company sent me Return Authorization, and I spent $14 (about 25% of the cost of the dash cam - so much for Prime membership) to return the dash cam plus all attachments to them for a replacement. Attaching that mount to the rear-view mirror was not easy, so I don't look forward to having to reattach it. However, I really hope the replacement will come quickly, have a functioning micro SD card slot and not have a defective lens or sensor (streaks).

UPDATE 3/1/2015 - Through Amazon I have requested a replacement dash cam since I am unable to insert a micro SD card fully into the slot, making the dash cam unusable. The Amazon description states that this dash cam has a one-year warranty.

Original review follows- from October 23, 2014, after I had it for about 2 weeks.
This works. However, the instructions only explain what options are available via the cam's menus. They do not explain HOW to use it.

The microSD - NOT mini-SD as others have mentioned - card will not stay in the camera by pushing it with my finger. I have to use a hard object. That's no longer a problem since I discovered how to transfer images to my computer - the instructions are not there in the booklet. (Plug in the USB cable that connects the dash cam to the computer, the dash cam turns on, and press the REC button - Image Capture utility pops up on my Mac computer.)

When I used the default settings - 720 and 60 fps - and I initially set it on my GPS platform on my dash, I got video that was upside down - but clear. Now I have it attached to the rearview mirror stem.

Unfortunately, the zoom is digital, not optical, resulting in extremely pixelated video. I was unable to read license tags or other details along the road (e.g., gas station prices).

The attachment to the mirror requires two hands and standing on my head to see where the cam attaches to the mount. And then, I have to be able to attach it without having the power cable disconnect. Also, I have to double check to ensure it is aimed properly.

It goes without saying that the cam has to be removed and hidden away when parking in a public place.

The fact that it comes on when the vehicle starts is nice. I have remote start, but the cam doesn't turn on until I unlock the door and insert the key and turn the ignition switch to its running position.

Considering the price, it is a good buy (especially compared to the GoPro cams). I may use it whenever I drive somewhere, but I may have to use 1080 resolution to read license tags of those idiots on the road who don't know how to drive.

UPDATE: Today (October 28, 2014) I used 1080p resolution. Now I was able to read the license tags of the vehicles that were not too far in front of me. Also, I was able to read signs on the sides of the road. The size of each 3-minute clip is about 290 MB. That's room for about 110 clips, each of which is 3 minutes long. Using longer clips is not advisable since each clip would be a large file. I see NO gap between one clip and the next.

One problem: Each and every video has a 'smear' which is either on the inside of the lens or on the sensor. Around the smear are several small spots. All of this is in the upper right, 3/10 of the way down and 3/10 of the way in from the right side. (I made a JPEG of an image divided into a 10x10 grid. The smear is in the 3rd segment from the top and 3rd from the right.) It is not enough for me to send it back, but it does tell us about the company's quality control.
text_fidelity_b: Wicked HD CARDVR1080PWHD4GB 1080p Car Camera & DVR Box (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Ubiquiti Networks Unifi 802.11ac Dual-Radio PRO Access Point (UAP-AC-PRO-US), Single,White I purchased two of these and their Cloud Key (CK). They come with good mounts but are attractive enough to just sit on a book case or shelf. The blue LED is a bit intrusive if installing in a dark room like a home theater, BUT using the CK, selecting the AP, then Configuration, you can disable it. Using the CK, the installation of new firmware, network configuration, general setup took less than an hour. The bulk of the time was doing the firmware updates and smoke testing.

My home is not big, 1500 sq. ft., but the 5G versus the 2.5 has a relatively small signal radius so I went with two at opposite sides of the house. If you want to benefit with the higher speeds plan accordingly. Meshing the two APs was painless and in my opinion requires little to no networking knowledge using the CK or downloading and installing their software. The CK is optional.

So far, no drops or sudden slow downs. Just solid performance. The unit today costs $130 USD. A great value for enterprise features and the option to integrate and provide further features with other Unifi products.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This little device came in handy during my recent trip to San Francisco, CA. I connected my Garmin nüvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator to my Toyota and it worked great. Installing and using this little machine is simple and easy. The instructions are easy to follow. I had a great time going to different places in San Francisco using this GPS and it never failed me. If you take a wrong route or direction, no problem, it will re-calculate and give the directions to get back on the right tack and keep driving. It works wonderfully. This has many features to help you get from point A to point B quickly and safely; features such as audible driving directions with text-to-speech (TTS), spoken street names, real-time traffic updates, and Internet connectivity for points-of-interest search, 5-inch resistive touch screen with colorful, animated map graphics and large easy-to-read screens are some of the coolest features. It comes complete with free lifetime map updates and traffic reports. The traffic reports are indicated pictorially using specific colors; red (heavy traffic), green (easy traffic) and yellow (moderate traffic). You do get a 3D junction view and speed limit indicators. If you are driving over the speed limit, the speed limit (e.g. 65 MPH), the display of 65 MPH goes red, if you are below the speed limit, it goes green.

It also offer robust point-of-interest (POI) search, including good category breakdowns, as well as searches that update in real time as you drive, complete with compass directions. When we were in Berkeley, CA, we were in an area which was completely new to us, and we wanted to go to an Indian restaurant and this feature helped us to find the nearest restaurant.

My brother uses GPS-enabled smart-phones and recommended me to go for GPS and I have never regretted buying this little gizmo, this offers good value for money.

Pros
* Big 5-inch screen
* Free lifetime traffic
* Pedestrian/public transit navigation
* Multi-destination routing
* Lane assist

Cons
* We had routing problems in some cases. It did not give the correct straight forward directions in my own home town. Once the satellite communication did not work when we are going to the airport.
* Traffic/lane info is available only in some cities
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

While the mount is plastic rather than metal, this keeps the lens weight down, which is always something that I appreciate. Despite being plastic the mount and housing are more than sturdy enough for even the most avid amateur photographer.

The image stabilization works very well and is an essential feature to have unless you have rock-steady hands.

I find the image quality to be excellent at all zoom ranges except for when it's at its max range, but even then it's more than acceptable.

It's certainly not the best lens that Canon makes, but I don't think there's another zoom out there that can match this performance at this price. It's a great second lens if you have a crop sensor body (such as the Rebel series) and the 18-55mm zoom (which is a common kit lens). The pair provides a wide range of shooting opportunities at a very reasonable cost. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 55-250mm f/4.0-5.6 IS II Telephoto Zoom Lens

Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras 48 LED unit - (since several items are listed under one product ID)
Positives:
- It is what it looks like, does what it claims to do, and basically works
- cheap
- comes with an AC adapter!! Wow. You can pay a lot for a light that doesn't

Negatives: I'm using this for Macro work (I'm new to macro) so that's the perspective I'm coming from
- Not Bright Enough! It's just not all that bright. Not enough to light a subject by itself for macro purposes. I doubt it's adequate for more than a highlight for portraiture. This is why 2 stars. If a light doesn't light - it's not a light.

Really that's it. This is not a knock to the light (and not why I gave it a low rating), but if you are planning on using it for macro, buy a flash instead. A flash will not only have higher output, but will help freeze the camera shake (a big macro problem). Also, I thought the full time light would be better for live insects (you can see what you're doing!), but it's the opposite. You need the flash to freeze action. Not a criticism (this light does not advertise itself as a flash), but something to know.

UPDATE: I used it a couple more times. I am finding it more useful than initially when very close in. I would still strongly recommend a flash for this unless you have a compelling reason for continuous illumination (e.g you're waiting for a bug to crawl into frame and it's too dark to see otherwise. Though the lights would probably scare the bug). If you have a pretty solid tripod setup, this can work for longer exposure macro. Not great though. Upped to 3 stars.

text_fidelity_a: Sonic Alert SB200SS Alarm Clock, Battery Backup | Wake with a Shake, Multicolored I am a chronic oversleeper and have tried every trick in the books with conventional alarms.  I've moved it across the room or under my bed so I have to get up to turn it off, I've changed the alarm noise every day to keep it annoying, I've set multiple alarm clocks, etc... Nothing worked until I bought this critter!  I've had it for a few months now and it continues to make me literally jump out of bed every morning.  The cord from the clock to the vibrating pod is fairly long, so I am able to put the pod under my fitted sheet and still put the clock a safe distance from my bed - just in case I do try to hit snooze.  It also has a super obnoxious beeping that you can activate with or without the vibrating, and you can change the intensity of the vibrating (keep your dirty jokes to yourself!).  It doesn't have radio, but that really doesn't bug me and the vibrating is strong enough that if I don't turn it off quick enough it will wake up my husband but those are the only two possible downsides I have noticed.  Be warned -  if you are just looking for a "fun" alarm clock, this is not for you.  This thing is seriously obnoxious and should only be purchased by the habitual oversleeper who has constantly proven that while sleeping they have the speed and prowess of a Cobra when it comes to silencing the average alarm clock.
text_fidelity_b: Sonic Alert SB200SS Alarm Clock, Battery Backup | Wake with a Shake, Multicolored

Cable Matters DisplayPort to DVI Adapter (DP to DVI Adapter) My desktop computer has a built in graphics card on the motherboard and I added a graphics card for gaming. The graphics card has a DVI, VGA and DisplayPort outputs. I had two monitors hooked up, one to the DVI, and one to the VGA port. I had another monitor (actually a TV) which duplicated screen two using a splitter. But I wanted to use it as a third separate monitor.

I tried several things to make a third monitor work: a DVI to HDMI cable (not an active cable) didn't work - the computer never saw the third monitor. I also tried the built in graphics card on the motherboard, plugging in an HDMI cable to its port and connecting the TV. That didn't work. it seems only one graphics card can be enabled at a time; either the one on the motherboard, or the installed graphics card.

This worked. As soon as I plugged it in, going from the displayport on the graphics card to the HDMI cable, the computer saw & recognized the 3rd monitor. Now I have three separate monitors.
text_fidelity_b: Cable Matters DisplayPort to DVI Adapter (DP to DVI Adapter)

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Pro Long story short I lost my airpod pros. Saw these on major discount ($90 for Black Friday), and couldn't resist. So here's my take in four parts. Sound Quality. Noise Cancelling. Ambient pass through. Features.

Sound quality -- versus the airpod pros, these are almost identical in sound. The only difference is the beats buds are a touch bass heavy. It's good, punchy bass, but noticeably more than the pros which were more balanced with its lows. So if you're a bass head, or hip-hop enthusiast, the beats win hands down.

Noise cancelling -- now this could have to do with the shape of my ear, but I found the beats to actually be a step ABOVE in noise cancelling. My gf still has her airpods and I compared. The seal the beat creates, paired with its noise cancelling makes it seem like the world doesn't exist. Beats win for me in NC.

Ambient pass-through -- this is where the beats lose out. Their noise cancelling is too good. So even when you have transparency turned on the world sound a little muddied out, while with the airpods, if I had transparency on it was almost like I wasn't wearing them. I miss that alot. So if you are in an environment where you need to hear what people are saying without removing your buds then airpods might be your pick. It's not to say that beats mak you deaf or anything but things are just noticeably quieter in transparance vs airpods with its full clarity.

Features -- another loss for the beats. They don't work with the beats app so no equalizer function... why beats???? WHY?? So you'll have to go third party if you want to equalize. The beats also won't stop the music or video you're watching if one falls out. No biggy for me as I like that but some people might not. Other than that it has similar functionality to airpods. One click to pause, two to skip, etc. It doesn't auto switch between devices but does actually switch pretty similarly. Takes maybe two clicks to switch it to my mac. The pairing is a breeze with iphones. Just open the case next to your iphone and voila. It's paired.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Pro

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung 32GB up to 48MB/s EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC Card with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM) Deciding to catch up on my product reviews – I was ELATED this particular Micro sD card is no longer available. I know that’s a bit mean-spirited, but I can’t help it. I was out the money for the item because it was past Amazon’s 30-day return window.

I purchased one in October of 2015 for my Samsung GS4, and only two (2) months later – I needed a brand new one. Why? It failed. No warning, nothing. Just a failure.

And this wouldn’t be the first failure either.

The sD card I bought in December failed as well, but I’ll give it up for it – It went OVER three (3) years before failing. It failed April 3, 2019. I remember that because of the event it failed during. I would’ve expected the failure when I transferred the sD card from the S4 to the S8 in May 2018, but the card still worked.

There were no signs of pending failure or issues. The night before (4/2), it worked and I was able to retrieve some photos off of it.

My mother and I went to Knott’s Berry Farm for the Boysenberry Festival. And, any photos take before we left – GONE. No error messages – just gone. I didn’t know until I got home.

What photos I have were the return photos from the drive home. I had briefly
glanced at the card data (on my phone) at about 2pm, but after that (without being dropped, banged, over-heated) the card failed. I know some will ask why I didn’t back them up – I was in transit, driving on the freeway, so it wasn’t feasible.

All I know is that my photos were gone.

So, I had to purchase another sD card for my phone. This time I chose the GREEN Evo Select one. And, from April 2019 to the date of this review, it’s been pretty solid. Though I’m not taking any chances. I store photos to my S8 as well as the sD card.

Since it isn’t available, I won’t bother with saying I don’t recommend it. I certainly won’t buy it again if it does become available again.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 32GB up to 48MB/s EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC Card with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM)

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming Works well if you can figure it out

I bought a Netgear EX6250 in a brick-and-mortar store about four months ago and my experience with it has been good overall...though not without its complications. Past experience with late-model Netgear products can be helpful in getting this unit set up and operating as the process is not always straightforward. It took me (who has a lot of experience with Netgear products and home networking in general) rather a few tries to get onto the right track in the Nighthawk app to set the thing up - you can run into roadblocks due to aspects of the Nighthawk app's design being less than intuitive (I know I did). I can't remember specifics now...so you know what I'm going to do? Out of lovingfriendliness for my fellow Amazon customers, I'm going to reset the extender to factory settings and set it back up, taking notes along the way, so that I can relate my experience more clearly and in greater detail.

Okay, so:

First you want to jump online and download the Netgear Nighthawk app to your phone. I don’t know if this unit can be set up without it.

Next, plug the extender into power - somewhere where it’s in range of your router. After you first plug the unit in, or after resetting it using the little recessed paperclip button on the side, the power LED will glow orange for rather a long time - two to three minutes in my experience - before finally turning green. Green means “go” - but orange doesn’t. So you just have to wait until that light turns green in order to be able to proceed with the setup process. Good opportunity to focus on the breath. And the fact that patience is a virtue.

Once the power indicator turns green, launch the Nighthawk app and check the little circle confirming that you accept Netgear’s terms and conditions and that you’ve read their privacy policy…even though you probably haven’t. Then tap “I Agree”.

On an iPhone, at least, the next screen says that iOS requires that you enable local network access in order to be able to set up your extender (which at this point the Nighthawk app is calling a “router” because it doesn’t yet know any better - you haven’t yet told it what you want to set up). Obviously, since you want to set up your extender, you’re going to okay that local network access. Tap “Continue” and your phone will ask you if you want to allow the app to find and connect to devices on your local network. Tap “OK”.

The next screen asks you to allow push notifications. This one’s up to you. I think I’ve always allowed them and I haven’t seen one yet, let alone been annoyed by excessive/unwanted notifications that are, in the end, just trying to sell me crap or otherwise waste my time.

The next screen tells you Netgear needs access to your device’s location services to automatically connect to your wifi network. I always allow this.

Next you’re told you have to create a new Netgear account or log into an existing one. Do that.

Then you’ll be asked if you want to enable Face ID and you’ll also be asked…something else I forget because I just blazed past it, momentarily forgetting that I was writing this detailed description of the process. But…y’know. You can read (because you’re reading this), so…tap the things on your screen that accord with your wishes. :)

At last we come to a screen that says, “Let’s set up your Nighthawk”, and tells you what to do if the unit’s been set up before. I don’t think I’ve ever had any luck using the “been set up before” option, so I always reset the extender to factory settings (by pressing and holding the paperclip/pen-point button on the side of the unit until the power light blinks orange) when I have a problem with the connection (which I seldom do, and when I do it’s usually because the power’s blinked or something else explicit has happened to make me need to set the extender up again). If this is your first time setting it up, tap “Set up a Nighthawk”. Even though I don’t think this extender is technically a Nighthawk. Doesn’t matter - you can still set it up with this app.

Next you’re shown a rundown of what’s going to happen. Read that as you’re inclined, then tap “Get Started!”.

On the product selection screen that comes up next, tap “Range Extender”.

The app tells you where to plug in your extender. Follow its instructions and tap “Next”.

The next screen just tells you to actually plug it in now, and wait (…and wait…and wait…) for a solid (green) power LED. Do that, and when you’ve got the solid green power light, tap “Next”.

On the next screen, the app will ask you to let it join your extender’s network. Tap “OK”, and wait while your phone connects to your extender. When it does, the screen will change to display “Great, we found your extender”. Tap “Next”.

Tap “Next” on the next screen as well.

Now your phone will look for your router’s network (which is your pre-existing wifi network, the one you want to extend). I think what it’s doing now is acting as a liaison between your router and the extender - introducing them to one another, as it were. Because what happens next is that your extender looks for and - ideally - connects to your wifi network. (When you’re asked to allow…something…to join your network, tap “Join”.)

And if all has gone well, that’s pretty much it. You’ll see a screen that says you’re up and running, and…there it is: you’re up and running!

Obviously, all of that is how things are *supposed* to go. If they go otherwise…you’ll probably need to be able to apply a searing laser beam of logic to the process and figure out how to make it work (that’s been my personal approach and, lucky for me, it’s always worked so far), or else to contact the dread Netgear Support People. I hope for your sake the laser beam works.

Good luck and enjoy!
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming

ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder Picked up a couple of these when Amazon had them on sale for half price. Had to return one because it was out of focus; Amazon processed the return quickly and the replacement works great.

Very pleased with the image quality of these cameras in the 1080p mode (which I always use). The video quality is sharp and colorful. Make sure you use the camera software to set the image quality to the highest level for best results.

Sound quality is a mixed bag. This camera uses noise reduction to reduce wind noise (which is a big problem with older Contour cameras at even moderate bicycling speeds), but the noise reduction also severely muffles your voice if you are trying to narrate a video while filming.

The camera controls are very easy to use, which is an improvement over earlier Contour cameras. The instant-on feature works great if you're filming only pieces of your event. I get about 3 hours of video from one battery charge. That also seems to be the amount of video that fits on a 32GB microSD card. If your event is longer than 3 hours, use the instant-on/instant-off feature to switch the camera on for just the important parts. The instant-on feature is a nice improvement over earlier Contour cameras that are difficult to turn on when you are moving.

Contour cameras seem to go on sale more often than GoPro. If you can catch it at a good sale price, I think Contour is a much better value than GoPro.
text_fidelity_b: ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder

Packaging: Easily unpackaged, not too excessive

Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount This TV makes me feel bad for ever having given another product 5 stars. It is really just about perfect. Instead of wasting a lot of space talking about the quality of the picture (believe me, it is there), I am going to concentrate on some finer points, particularly those real and perceived weak points:

(This is replacing a 2009 Sony Z-Series TV, which I also love and still consider a fantastic TV; it was the first year of Internet-capable TVs if I remember correctly, and I used the DLNA features with Universal Media Server, but could never get a Plex profile to work right, so I am happy to have a newer TV that supports Plex via App, besides for the 4k, HDR, etc., etc. I have a bunch of other TVs scattered about, but the other two I use most are less expensive Samsung Smart models from five or so years ago.)

Back to (possible) negatives:

I wasn't sure I would like the stand and style. I always hated those Samsung TVs with the plastic grey legs, and I thought this would look too much like that. I thought my ideal stand was either a perfect 90-degree version of the Sony A1E, or perhaps the A8F, which I had my eye on due to its very low profile, minimalist stand. Anyway, this one looks so much better in real life than I expected. It's actually metal, and fairly dark. Placed on low furniture, it looks great walking by, and sits at the right height while watching. I guess it is made to fit a Sony sound bar perfectly (I use full surround setup, so I don't care). But I am much, much happier with the looks than I thought I would be. If that is your hesitation, go check it out in a store (before coming back for the right price).

Thickness: its thicker than some, including last year's 930E, but the way it angles out from the back gives a much sleeker appearance than you may expect just from looking at the dimensions. You only see its thickness at about 80 degrees to the side. Overall, it sits back far and takes up little extra room than it has to. The TV looks as great off as it does on.

I read a professional review that mentioned the picture doesn't look as good from a side angle. I guess that's true, but it's not nearly as drastic of a change as it sounded from the review. In fact, one of the best TV seats in my house is about 30-degrees off-center, and I don't see a difference from there at all. At 45-degrees, you start to see a difference.

Above mentioned professional review also mentioned the Android TV thing can be a little clunky. I don't feel it, to be honest. It's been nothing but good surprises for me. One thing that could be improved is customization of your home screen. You can re-order some apps, but I haven't figured out how to delete the shortcuts for stuff that isn't even downloaded. And I'm never going to play goofy games on my TV (besides real video games), so how can I get rid of that whole section that is taking up space. You can block recommended content, so after them pushing some crapware on you initially, you can basically run add-free. Looks like you'll probably have to sign in to Google, though, but you can make a new account just for your TV (which is what I do for every device).

The downward facing ports look really good with the cable management, so good that I really don't want to use any of the side inputs for permanent setups. For that reason, they should have put the IR blaster and composite input facing down as well (not that I need them, as I don't have cable, but some people will).

Not that I even checked my link speed, but manual says Ethernet port is 100mbps. Can't imagine you'll ever need more than that unless you expect to run uncompressed video without a converter.

The remote is nicer than I expected, but still not as nice as my old one. Plus, although it has Bravia Sync, it doesn't easily just control my stereo the way I would like it to (as my old Sony TV did).Not sure why there has to be a Google button on the remote. Or even Netflix. These should be programmable. Actually, four programmable Apps and/or Input buttons would be greatly appreciated in their place.

That's about it for nitpicking. Here's some things that are totally awesome (besides all the obvious):

It can read all commonly used containers for video files, including *mkv, and it can decompress 4k HEVC (H.265) video natively. So even though my NAS cannot transcode 4k on the fly, if I set it to run at full quality, the TV does it just fine! And since H.265 was made because of 4k video, here's hoping we don't have formats this TV can't play any time soon. This is just fantastic to me, as I really love my NAS' Plex server function. You can also play up to 4k H.265 video right off a hard drive via USB.

My UMS media server is showing up under Video devices (which is where the DLNA servers show up), but you can't see the files. I haven't messed with it much (because now I don't care), but I assume they'll get a profile working before long.

I love the built-in TV guide function and also the way you can browse other channels along the bottom of your screen without changing the channel. These are both great features (the TV guide function on my old TV was abandoned after a few years, but I expect this one will continue to operate). I do not have or want cable, so now I have the features that are nice to have with cable without the burden of slow response cable boxes and the burden of dealing with Comcast.

I haven't even tried out the professional settings (or even messed with anything but motionflow) because the TV is impressing me every second it's on. Again, as this is the first 4k TV to reside in my house, I guess I should be amazed. But the blacks as bars on movies wider than 16:9 are so black you don't notice them. Space scenes are to die for. 4k is done right here: this is the high end of quality, about the only thing worth removing my old Z-series for. I just love it. It looks amazing on and off, and does everything I want it to do (mainly Plex, and Netflix is nice now and then as well). I'm so happy that Plex works so well with this TV without an expensive NAS upgrade, even with movies encoded at 2160p and 7.1 surround. Just fantastic.

It's better than I expected even from Sony's almost-second-to-flagship model. About as high end as they come before they jump up drastically in price. I wouldn't have anything less on my primary TV stand, and I don't need anything more. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount

text_fidelity_a:
Byron Statics Portable CD Boombox with AM/FM Radio, Top Loading CD, 1W RMS x 2 Stereo Speaker, Aux-in Jack, LCD Display, AC110-120V Operated (KBB-250) I’m old enough to remember the old 8-track players, but growing up my media player was of course a cassette player, and sometimes a “dual” player.

But, in 1995, I opted to transition to CDs. By that time they were a bit more affordable, though the average $17.95 felt like it was anything but.

By around 2005, I was transitioning to an MP3 player. The first one was a literal BRICK (Creative Nomad).

And, by 2008, I had an iPod Nano. By 2011, I had the iPod classic. Even my 2008 Chevy had an aux port to connect my iPod to. So, I really had NO need of a CD player. After all, most of my music was on my computer or iPod. Living in an apartment is NOT ideal for a “stereo”. I wouldn’t want to hear someone else’s music, so I don’t think they’d want to hear mine.

When I saw this, I decided to get it.

It is COMPACT, no frills, no remote control. In fact there is only a “selection” button, not a (back track or forward track).

I haven’t tried the radio function yet. The CD top loader consists of a manual opening (no push-button), and the CD has to be popped in and out manually. The sound is pretty decent for the size of the unit. This is more for desktop or bedside use. Definitely not for a home “sound system”.

I then tested the AUX cable for the iPod and the sound was the same as the CD. That feature was REALLY easy to use.

It is a pretty solid, light-weight unit. I do believe it could be a bit cheaper. I wouldn’t mind getting a second one should the price drop.
text_fidelity_b: Byron Statics Portable CD Boombox with AM/FM Radio, Top Loading CD, 1W RMS x 2 Stereo Speaker, Aux-in Jack, LCD Display, AC110-120V Operated (KBB-250)

text_fidelity_a:
OCTA Spider Monkey - Secure Height Adjustable Stand for iPad, Galaxy, Surface and All Tablets for Desk, Bed, Car, Couch Do I like the Spider Monkey? Yes... with reservations. First let me cover why I like it. I read in bed, and I spend a lot of time switching hands, trying to find ways to prop my book or tablet up, shaking feeling back into my fingers. And then, when I fall asleep, which I always do, the tablet might end up under me or might end up on the floor, and neither is good. The Spider Monkey gives me a way to prop up my tablet without holding it, and to keep it out of my way when I fall asleep.

The downside? How it works depends very much on what you attach it to. I have a headboard that allows me to twist and anchor the tail in a lot of ways, but it doesn't always hold the tablet in position. It can swing around, and be difficult to angle for good reading. Also? It's not all that easy to put together. Once you do, it'll hold, but until then you may find yourself screaming in frustration.

In spite of the drawbacks, though, the Spider Monkey has been a real boon to my reading. If I work with it a bit, it'll even hold my kindle in its cover. I'm not sure I think it's worth $80, to be honest. Half that seems fair to me.

Disclaimer: I received this product in exchange for an honest review.
text_fidelity_b: OCTA Spider Monkey - Secure Height Adjustable Stand for iPad, Galaxy, Surface and All Tablets for Desk, Bed, Car, Couch

text_fidelity_a:
AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA Ok I can be a bit of a headphone snob, but at a near $300 price point I have some pretty high expectations. I ran them through my standard audio tests and these passed every one with flying colors. Bottomline, where most wireless sets fail is with bass, either its lacking or they overcompensate for it at the expense of everything else. (I'm talking to you SkullCandy). These however managed to be astounding on bass without it being overwhelming. Deep rich sounds, but mid and upper still came in crystal clear. It was impressive.

They also manage to have noise canceling without the annoying hiss present in the high end SkullCandy set I recently reviewed. The AKG's are superior and even performed better than my beloved, but admittedly old Sennheisers. How they would match up against a newer pair I can't say though, I will fangirl all day over a high end set of Senn's, but these AKGs give them some serious competition.

The ambient pass-through was a welcome addition, and these paired effortlessly via blue tooth. The ear cups were comfortable, although warm like every other pair of closed noise-canceling headsets I've tried. I will be honest I tend to prefer an open headset, but that is more preference than anything to do with this set. The ear cups were smaller than other pairs I've worn, I'm petite so that wasn't an issue but if you got yourself some good sized ears keep that in mind.

So if you have $300 burning a hole in your pocket and need some very well balanced wireless headphones, I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA

Epica Digital Emergency Solar Hand Crank AM/FM/NOAA Radio, Flashlight, Smartphone Charger with NOAA Certified Weather Alert & Cable-ONE Cable Does All This is one of those products that is good to have, but even better if you never need to use it since you'll probably be using it when the electricity is out. It offers a lot of functionality in a compact size: a flashlight, AM radio, FM radio and weather band radio. It runs off of an internal rechargeable battery that is kept charged either via solar power, USB connection or by cranking the handle. It can also serve as a source to charge a cell phone (albeit with very limited capacity to do so since the internal battery is only rated at 800mAh).

It works pretty well. The flashlight is very bright - had no problems lighting my way down a dark stairway and in a totally dark room. The radio is OK. The reception is spotty and it only picked up a few of the very strong stations in the area. It's very susceptible to positioning - moving it just a couple of inches turned a clear station into static.

Cranking the handle to keep it charged is pretty easy. It turns easily and the handle is comfortable. According to the manual, one minute of cranking equals 30 minutes of flashlight use or 20 minutes of radio use.

This is a good product to keep on hand in case of emergency, such as a bad storm or extended power outage. It won't keep you cool in the summer or warm in the winter, but at least you can see where you're going and listen to the radio. Definitely worth a spot in the emergency kit. The only shortcoming is the somewhat limited radio reception.
[sample provided by manufacturer for review]
text_fidelity_b: Epica Digital Emergency Solar Hand Crank AM/FM/NOAA Radio, Flashlight, Smartphone Charger with NOAA Certified Weather Alert & Cable-ONE Cable Does All
