text_fidelity_a:
jumper EZbook 3 Pro Windows 10 Laptop 13.3" FHD Bezel-Less, Intel Slim Ultrabook Portable, 6GB RAM 64GB ROM, Metal Shell Lightweight Notebook Update: I do really like this computer. It has smoothly integrated into my home network and I now quickly go to it for quick and easy browsing and/or controlling stuff in my house (particularly if the main computer is in use by somebody else or for some reason tethered. The great thing is that with the full power of Windows and third party software, it can be whatever you need it to be. The one negative I've found, though, is that the delete key is under the backspace key where you expect backslash to be (which is in turn beside the right alt key). For this reason, I've accidentally went into sleep mode a few times, which is annoying. You can turn off the power key (while running) in windows, but the delete key still isn't where it is supposed to be.

Original review:

Surprise! I actually love this computer.

I mean, I am a bit of a power user, so I have a big gaming laptop and a couple of servers throughout my house, not to mention a few purpose-built niche laptops. So while I was a bit skeptical of this machine before it came since I saw the low price tag, I think it's awesome for the right purpose.

I mean, I totally get what "Chrome Books" are trying to do - be low price, low weight computers that run basically "from the cloud". But who really wants a computer running Android? I mean, there are phones for that. So running Windows 10 is a great idea. (Not that I love Windows 10, but if you install Windows Classic Shell and tweak, tweak, tweak away...turn off all permissions, get rid of all the stupid crap they're trying to sell you, use an offline account, then it is almost as good as Windows 7).

Anyway, you don't get a lot of fancy new stuff, but what you do get is important: 1080p screen, mini-HDMI out (odd choice, would have gone for micro or even full, but whatever), 2 USB 3.0 (No C), a micro-SD card reader, headphone jack, and a M.2 expansion port.

64GB of ROM is pretty small, but they installed so little bloatware (just one program to make the touchpad better - I uninstalled it because I didn't recognize it, am paranoid, and figure I can adjust it with whatever is built into Windows) that you have ~45GB free. Should be enough for stuff like MS office and other junk you may want. But you know what, I have a 36TB NAS, and Windows works flawlessly with it, so if I'm using this as a home machine, it's not a problem. I don't much care for public cloud, so if I want to take this on the road, I can always stream (usually still reach my NAS) or just throw in an SSD (by the way, it only takes the small form factor) or a giant micro-SD card (although admittedly either of these factors takes away the fact that this item is inexpensive to begin with.

6GB of RAM is sufficient for a computer that is not meant to be a workhorse.

It's really thin and light and with a real keyboard is just delightful as opposed to dealing with a tablet; a tablet always disappoints me when I'm trying to get something done quickly. It also boots up fast due to NAND memory. It doesn't even look cheap or anything. It actually looks pretty good.

It has a regular "wall wart" type AC adapter instead of the usual laptop power brick. I like this, but the cord is a little short (on the other hand, it is likely easily replaced with something in my electronics closet) The barrel adapter goes into the right side of the device (which is not abnormal, but less normal than the back or the other side in my experience) and the unfortunate part is that it will partially fit into the stereo mini-plug port for headphones on the same spot on the other side, which is likely to cause some confusion.

The only apparent downside is that the keyboard seems...like it vibrates slightly. Like it's not held in tight enough or something. I mean, it does have nice keys and overall I like it, but it just feels slightly weird, although still much better than a tablet roll-out keyboard.

I actually really like this little machine. Not for my main computer or my only computer, but definitely for easy browsing, or a multimedia machine for a teen, or a school computer, a travel computer, whatever. I'd use it for plenty of things, happily.

If you're cool with the memory - and living off a NAS, an SD card, or the cloud - and you're looking for something small and usable, definitely give this some consideration.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) The Fire HD 10 tablet is pretty much an unbeatable deal for a tablet these days. You get a really good display and decent processor and memory for a great price---especially when it's on sale. And the Fire OS (a rebranded and modified version of Android) works smoothly.

A trade-off is a not-so-good camera resolution.

And there are some limitations on what you can do. If you already own some Android apps, you might not find them in the Amazon app store, and those you do will not credited as paid for. You'll have to buy them again (if you choose to buy).

One option is to follow online instructions for installing the Google Play Store on your Fire. But that's kind of iffy. You don't know when the next Fire OS update might break that installation. And Play Store might download updates to some of the core Fire OS apps that might conflict with proprietary Fire OS modifications.

Another consideration is that this device serves as an advertising and sales platform for Amazon. It's tailored for that. Something to keep in mind.

The thing to consider is if you can be happy with what Amazon gives you. If you're going to be trying to root and work around the OS and app store limitations soon after you get it, maybe it's worth just getting an Android tablet and foregoing the Fire.

If you can be happy with all that, overall it's a great deal for a capable tablet.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 2 camera kit This was a real disappointment. One of the main problems is that it is only compatible with 2G and if you have a 2G and a 5G network it still may not work if your network is merged and/or you have intermittent 2G. Not sure if this applies to you? It probably does if you live in the United States in a major city. Secondly the support was terrible. Have you ever call a support line and it took 20 minutes just for them to get your name your email and whatever other information they claimed they need to identify its you? Well that's exactly the type of support you can expect from Blink. They take forever and I'm not exaggerating, forever to even get to your question which they probably won't answer because they are too busy reading from their script while they ignore your questions. Don't waste your time, your money or your very sanity. Take a hard pass on this.

Update 6/10/20:
Received an email from Alex with Amazon Executive Support. Apparently the information that we received regarding our 2g/5g internet was not valid. However using an extension cord a long one we positioned the sync module closer to our wifi modem and were finally able to set up the camera. And did get it online. However, that was all.

First of all the 2 year battery life that the description touts is just plain misleading. Apparently this camera will provide that type of battery life if you only arm the camera when you are not at home and have the settings on the lowest functionality, e.g. lowest video quality, lowest sensitivity, shortest video length etc.

Even on the highest settings we the camera just does not "CONSISTENTLY" capture video of motion or people period. Comparing this camera to our blink door bell we are getting about 10% or less video capture of motion/people. However, it does capture video when there is no apparent motion and/people in the activity zones. Also some videos are for 3 seconds or less for who knows what reason.

Not sure why Blink would think that anyone would be happy with this camera and not sure what type of situation this camera would work in since it does not do what it says it does.

This camera is a mystery and is not user friendly. Support is a joke. We have spent so much time trying to figure this camera out it is ridiculous. The Ring camera door bell is much much much easier and 100 times more reliable. We are definitely sending this back.
text_fidelity_b: Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 2 camera kit

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Powershot S2 IS 5MP Digital Camera with 12x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (OLD MODEL) I have only had this camera a few weeks but it has met all my expectations--I got it to photograph jewelry and small artwork primarily, at which it excels. I am also am finding it does a great job on a lot of other kinds of shots. I find I enjoy photographing birds--a tough subject--and have gotten some nice shots of them with this camera. The controls are easy to operate, conveniently located, and pretty easy to figure out even without resorting to the manual. I'm still doing a lot of experimenting with different settings to "learn" the camera's capabilities and get a feel for its sensitivity to light and its optics...an exercise highly recommended for folks like me who are new to cameras with manual controls. Have taken a few video clips with it that came out great.

The memory card it came with is kind of a joke--I bought a Kingston 2 GB card to use instead and have been real happy with that. It writes super-fast and I come nowhere close to ever running out of room (but I delete a lot of shots, too). Also, rechargeable batteries are HIGHLY recommended. I have three sets...one set lasted for three weeks of casual use--even with the LCD often open.

I've added a 52mm adapter tube and a few filters, plus a hood. Mainly I wanted the adapter and a UV filter to protect the lens for tight super-macro shots. One of these days I might get a wide angle lens. If you're going to be doing macro stuff or using the zoom a lot, use of a tripod will be key in getting clearly focused shots.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Powershot S2 IS 5MP Digital Camera with 12x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (OLD MODEL)

The main positives - the BT connectivity is excellent and zero loss of signal while jogging/yard work etc. Never had to repair the earbuds to my phone (Note). Battery life is as advertised and very pleasing. Fit is comfortable and no heaviness or blocked feeling.

The could-be-better - getting used to the stem controls is not that easy and has been finicky at times. Volume/bass is mediocre at best. Though some noise reduction is perceivable, it is uneven. It is IPX5 rated, means it should be able to "resist a sustained, low-pressure water jet spray".

At the advertised price, you are paying really for the battery life, BT chip, above-average noise suppression and average sound. Overall, a decent pair for using in situations where you are OK sacrificing performance (travel, yard work, jogging etc - where one could lose or step on it ).

It is not a desk but a stand that sits atop a desk. It will provide the benefits of a standing desk without the expense and commitment.

The directions are pictorial, something I do not like. They lead to some confusion but then again I am a person who prefers words to illustrations. That being said the installation was not as frustrating as I anticipated.It seems sturdy. Adjusting the stand itself is simple and smooth. Ho weer adjusting the monitors requires fussing with bolts and tools. The work surface is adequate though not especially generous. there is a little wobble when typing in both the raised and lowered position but not enough to be a deal breaker. It doesn't seem completely level though I haven't determined whether it is the desk or the stand. Visually they both seem okay and I assume this is the stand as I"ve not experienced it with other things.

I have chronic back problems and try to get up at least every hour when I am office bound. This desk does help increase standing time. It is easy to work in the standing position, which is somewhat of a surprise . I am still undecided about upgrading to a complete standing desk but am enjoying the benefits by using this stand.
text_fidelity_b: Ergotech Freedom Stand, Includes Single Monitor Stand, Adjustable Sit Stand Desk 30" Wide, 0-13.2lb weight capacity, 13"-30" Monitor size, VESA compatible 75x75, 100x100, Black

Soundcore by Anker Life Q30 Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Multiple Modes, Hi-Res Sound, Custom EQ via App, 40H Playtime, Comfortable Fit, Bluetooth Headphones, Multipoint Connection These are very good travel headphones. Over-the-ear style is very comfortable when worn for hours at a time. The headphones are relatively lightweight and compact. They fold nicely into the included EVA soft-shell case, which fits easily into my carry-on bag.

The headphones pair easily with my Android smartphone. The Soundcore smartphone app is required for upgrading the headphones' firmware. The app also lets you customize the equalization to one of the presets or you can design your own. Depending on the kind of music you are listening to, the equalizer can make a noticeable difference in clarity and balance.

Unfortunately, the app spams me with notifications about unrelated Anker products. Hopefully this will not be frequent.

Noise cancellation works well. There are 3 modes: on, off (normal), and transparency that lets you talk to people around you without taking the headphones off. Noise cancellation can be toggled both from the app and from a button on the headphones themselves.

Overall, sound quality is good. More of a balanced sound than the boomy default effects that some headphones give. I mostly listen to acoustic music, so this works well for me. Clarity is good. Bluetooth connectivity has been great so far.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore by Anker Life Q30 Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Multiple Modes, Hi-Res Sound, Custom EQ via App, 40H Playtime, Comfortable Fit, Bluetooth Headphones, Multipoint Connection

text_fidelity_a:
Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray This Honeywell smart home security starter kit has a great video and is easily expandable.

When opening the box I was pleased to see that it was packaged very well. The box even has a magnetic closure. Maybe a little over the top but a nice feature to make it feel like more of a luxury product. I also have the Honeywell thermostat and that box wasn’t as nice.
Each item in the security kit was simple and clear to find since they were labeled in their own little box. There is an instruction sheet that is quite large for the info that it holds. The instructions have nice graphics and it is spaced out well so it is very easy to read. The instructions are simple for initial set up. Though I would appreciate another manual to help with the “extra” things it can do. I relied on the Honeywell videos and reviews (video and written) by other people to get it functioning with all the bells and whistles. I could see the need for a manual for those less tech savvy.

The base station could be a little smaller but it looks very nice in my kitchen and blends in very well. It’s a nice design with only one button, for the speaker. You can touch the top to check how it is working and run your finger around the top to change the volume. The camera is small and has a privacy ring that can be twisted to block the camera. It would be a nice feature if I could twist the camera from the app in case we forgot to open it when we left.
The middle mesh part is the speaker and it has a good range of volume and the sound is good.
The bottom has a light inside and it changes colors when you choose the different settings. It also lights up to help when you set up new devices.
The base has a backup battery. You will get an alert when it doesn’t have power. This has been handy when there is a storm so I know when the power goes out and when it is restored.

To start the set up I downloaded the Honeywell app. It was easy to use and is a nice looking app. The main page is very simple. When you go to the settings that’s where all the extras are.
My husband also has the app on his phone so he can use it just as I can.
Set up was very easy besides having troubles with it connecting it to my WiFi. I decided to wait till the next day and it worked after a couple tries. I don’t have a fast internet so that might be why. I haven’t had any issues with the connection since set up. Besides the WiFi wait it was about 15 minutes to set up the app and base.
The key fob was very easy to pair up and only took me a couple minutes to have it ready to use. Nice to have when a babysitter comes over.
The access sensors were very easy to install and set up. I didn’t need the extra piece. It only took me a few minutes to stick them on and pair them. I did use painters tape to attach them to my doors and frames. I am worried about the tape they have ruining my stained trim. I haven’t seen any comments about it. I also wanted to try it on other doors and windows first.
When you open a door or window in home mode it chimes and sends you an alert. When you open in away mode it will sound the alarm. I wish the door sensors were a little smaller or gray. They stand out too much on my wood trim and door. If my trim was white they wouldn’t be very noticeable.

The camera is very clear and has a wide angle so if you position it right you can see a lot. You can switch the video to full screen and the picture is still good. You are also able to zoom in on the video in the app and it has options to take a snap of the video, talk through the base or have an alarm go off. Sometimes it takes a while for the video to load or it will just turn off. I am assuming this is from my slower internet. Usually after a few tries I can get it to work. Also there is a delay in the video and the movement is jumpy, this could be due to the slower internet also. You still get a good picture of who is there. I was impressed with the night vision.

The motion detection is a nice feature when you are away. I have been trying to figure out the best setting while we are at home. It will send me alerts all the time when we are home. Most of the alerts are during the people detection time. Maybe because our camera covers so much of our main area. I do like that how the people detection can let me know who is in the house and I don’t have to look at the video. When it detects motion it will take a short video clip and save them below the live video. You can scroll down to look at the older ones. It looks like the clips are saved for a day. The people detection is limited to 2 hours. But I did notice that you could set it for the morning then when that time was over you could change it for later in the day. You would have to remember to change it but good to know if you wanted it on for longer or multiple times in the day. Not sure why they don’t have an option for more time.

The geofencing didn’t work well for me. It would switch to away mode even when the phone was close to it. We’ve decided to turn that feature off. It’s easy enough to turn it to away with the app, key fob, or talk to it. We are at home a lot so it makes more sense to do it manually. But I could see it being a great feature for people gone more during the day.

The kids like the Alexa feature that it comes with. They can ask the weather, time, kids jokes. I use it for the timer and to ask it questions. We had problems with playing songs. It wanted us to subscribe to amazon music. We have found other ways of playing music but it’s not very easy. Alexa seems limited but still useful. This is my first Alexa enable device so hard to compare.

I like that the security base links to my Honeywell thermostat (it was very easy to pair it) and I can tell Alexa to turn it off or change the temperature or use the same app. I would like to get other devices that link to it. This is a great starter kit and I like that it is expandable for your needs.

You are able to do two way taking with the app. It’s not always easy to understand and you have to talk slower.

The box says you get free 24-hour cloud storage. I’m not sure if that’s for the video clips or what you are actually storing. I haven’t found where the cloud is accessed.

Overall it is easy to use and looks nice. It’s nice that you can have a security system that is easy to use and it doesn’t have a monthly fee. I don’t usually need all the security features that this security system offers but it’s nice to have it set up and ready for when I do.
text_fidelity_b: Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray

They have got more comfortable. I don't use them often so I don't think it's my ears that have got used to them I think the material has gotten softer with use and maybe the band has stretched out a bit.

I'll add to my review that while these are not hard to drive they are not easy to drive either. They are near the top of easy to drive. They are 32 ohms and sensitivity is 96db. What does that mean? I use these mostly with my computer that has a pretty good sound chip and I find that I have to have the computer sound (windows 7) and the music app (foobar 2000) volume all the way up to get these to where they open up and sound best. In general, they need to be a little louder than I would like to sound their best.

Sound wise I find myself punching up the bass a bit. They need a little bit more hit and a touch of bloom for things like the bass guitar and kik drum to sound about right. Not a lot, just a 3db boost from about 80 to 200hz. I also find they need a bit of a push at 10K and up to put a little more air around the instruments. With more listening, I'm not quite as thrilled with the sound as I was, but I still like them. Hours of listing do not leave me with ear fatigue and they do not punish poorly recorded music.

Update after a month:
These have not got more comfortable and I kinda wish I had returned them but for $32 it's not really worth it given I'd get charged $5 for the return. These hurt after a couple of hours and no amount of moving them around relieves it. The material is soft enough but I think it is too soft and packs down. Also clamping pressure is pretty high on my melon so now that I'm keeping them I may try to stretch them out a bit

================================================================

I am FUSSY about sound! I want natural neutral sound. That's what you get with these. The bass is natural, drums sound pretty good. Sibilance is there but not annoying. They are accurate without being clinical or fatiguing. They are musical without being over warm or polite. They do not punish poorly recorded music like some more HiFi headphones do. There is a nice amount of 'air' around the instruments but not much of a sound stage beyond that. They are a nice middle of the road set of headphone, not too bright, but bright enough, a good mid-range, pretty well-controlled bass without much bleed and some bass extension. They could use a touch more bloom to suit my tastes but what is there suits me fine. If I thought they were bass shy I would tell you.

I use a 15 band equalizer on my computer and I end up putting some EQ on most headphones I use, but I found with these I liked them best with no EQ. They do not go super loud with my phone. Loud enough for me, but not might be loud enough if you like your music really loud.They need a little volume to sound there best but that's pretty typical and I have had headphones that needed to be louder to sound their best.

They have one big problem. They are not very comfortable. I would not get these if wearing them all day at work is your thing of if comfort is really important to you because you get annoyed if they are not comfortable. In comparison, the Sennheiser HD 2.20 is WAY more comfortable. The foam is too thin and you almost feel like the plastic is pressed against your ears. They 2nd day they felt a little better. My ears getting used to them, or maybe the foam adapting to the shape of my ears or a little bit of both.The headband cushion is also really thin but did not bother me as much as the earpieces.

They have almost no isolation. My old open back Sennheiser 239 had more isolation. I'm also not a fan of how round that headband is but I guess they did that so they would fold up smaller? I don't know but I wish the fit a little closer to the head on the sides.

The cable is kind of weird in that the right and left cords are side by side like lamp cord and a little thicker than on other budget headphones.

Between my old Senn 239, and the Senn 2.20 and the Jabra Move (I think it was the Move) I like the sound of these Shure the best by far. If these cost $50 or even $60 I'd be really happy with these, at least for sound. For $30 dollars I'm REALLY happy with them.

I'd be tempted to knock a star off for comfort but for me, the sound is everything so the 5 stars are for the sound.
text_fidelity_b: Shure SRH145m+ Portable Collapsible Headphones with Remote + Microphone Compatible with All Apple iOS Devices

I wanted something to give my aging ears a bit more volume when I need t. I also wanted to be able to share what I was listening to with visitors using additional headphones.

I found the HA400 to serve both purposes admirably. I put it into 24 hours of continuous service just after receiving it. It worked beautifully in boosting the volume when needed it. In addition, visitors found it useful to be able to adjust their individual headphone volumes.

I haven't actually measured the dynamic range of the HA400 yet, but this past weekend's experience makes me believe it is excellent within the boundaries of the levels that come out of the headphone jack of my receiver. I noticed no distortion during operation.

I believe the HA400 is a good choice cost-effective choice for amplifying and splitting a single audio stream into four headphone-level stereo channels.

Be aware that it requires 1/4" stereo plugs to mate with. You will need adapters if you have cords with 1/8" plugs. The unit comes with a wall wart power supply with a generous length of output cable. There is no ON/OFF switch.

FWIW, I'll be ordering one or two more HA400s for use with our home entertainment equipment. I ordered this unit from Amazon on another account, hence no "Verified Purchase" notation. The price was competitive and delivery reasonable.
text_fidelity_b: Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver

When I plugged it in, again, there seemed to be no power... and then suddenly there was a burning smell and smoke coming from the enclosure where the power supply went in. It was quite scary, because I almost did not catch it soon enough.
I took a long shot and contacted the company anyways, even though it had been such a while to explain the long ordeal, and why I had not contacted sooner... Among my sickness, I was giving the device the benefit of the doubt, because I honestly thought it was my pc.
This is the message I received in return "In this case, it is highly commended to stop using this hard drive enclosure.
According to your information, this item is faulty. Regarding our products, a 12-month warranty is provided, however, it is obviously that the item ordered on 2016 has been far beyond its warranty. Hope that you could understand."
They did offer a 15% "return after purchase" discount refund if I would purchase a new one. But, as I am disabled, I cannot afford to do that at this time.
Hopefully, my backup really is on the hard drive that this unit supposedly saved it to that one time, as some beloved photos of my deceased father are on there, and I don't have them anywhere else.
I wish I were more tech savvy and didn't stay sick so much... Even so, I wouldn't have known the problem until I got a new pc anyways. Based on my experience and other reviews, I would not recommend this enclosure to anyone.
I do hope this helps someone.
text_fidelity_b: Inateck 3.5 Hard Drive Enclosure, Aluminum USB 3.0 Sata HDD Enclosure, FE3001
